title: Pager sidelines playbook (personal draft)
body:
Purpose: quick, portable set of notes to cover short pager stretches from home, coffee shop, or train. Not a canonical runbook — keep this shallow and actionable.

Top-level goals (my priorities while covering):
- Keep customer-facing latency < 300ms P95 for API v2 routes (asia + eu).
- Keep error-rate < 0.5% for generation endpoints; if not possible, failfast and swap to fallback model.
- Triage fast, escalate to on-call SRE if infra or k8s control-plane looks unhealthy.

Quick status checks (first 2 minutes)
- Grafana: open "Prod Overview" -> look at request rate / token/sec & 5m error rate.
  Link: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/prod-overview
- Check alert inbox: Slack #pager-alerts -> skim recent alerts, click INC links.
- Kubernetes: kubectl get pods -n inference | grep -v Running (watch for CrashLoopBackOff).
  Common commands: kubectl -n inference get pods | egrep "gateway|worker|cache"
- Queue depth: redis-prod: INFO keyspace, or look at Kinesis backlog metric on dashboards.

Common alert fingerprints (fast heuristics)
- Spike in 503s + gateway CPU at 95% -> likely inference-gateway saturation. Temporary mitigation: set-service-weight to fallback-light model and open a capacity incident.
- KV cache NPE in worker logs -> check recent deploys (CI MR id included below), restart affected pods.
- Embeddings lag (high latency but low error) -> likely model host in different AZ; route to eu region instance or enable cross-region fallback.

Temporary actions (short-lived "workarounds")
- Scale: kubectl scale deployment inference-gateway --replicas= N (be conservative + coordinate via #sre on Slack).
- Swap model route: curl -XPOST https://api.redwood.ai/admin/routes/swap -d '{"route":"/v2/generate","model":"redwood-compact-v1"}' (use admin token). Only do if you can confirm capacity shortage.
- Restart sequence: restart gateway -> wait 45s -> restart workers (avoid restarting all at once).

Escalation matrix (who to ping)
- First SRE: Diego Martínez (Slack @diego) — infra control-plane, k8s, autoscaler
- Second engineer: Priya Rao — serving runtime internals, model kernel crashes
- Product contact for major customer impact: Renee Wong

Notes to self / mental checklist while on call
- Leave a short Slack summary AFTER any action: what I changed, why, and how to roll back.
- If I open an INC: include top 3 logs + full pod describe + last deploy MR number.
- Mark issues with tag "pager-fixme" in GH if quick patch needed, but avoid on-call code pushes unless approved.

Known rough commands (my annotated cheat-sheet)
- tail logs from gateway: kubectl -n inference logs -f deploy/inference-gateway | sed -n '1,200p'
- describe failing pod: kubectl -n inference describe pod <pod-name>
- fetch last 2k lines from worker: kubectl -n inference logs <pod> -c worker --tail=2000
- check autoscaler: kubectl -n infra get hpa

Open questions / TODO (for next revision)
- Add a small play for model-variant fallback that includes safe rate-limits (avoid storming the fallback pool).
- Collect a short list of reproducer prompts for worker NPEs (ask Priya).
- Clean up the admin route swap API call (need proper curl snippet with header).

Personal reminders (notes-to-self)
- If paged while out: respond within 5-10m with at least a status update.
- If I had to manually swap routes or scale, create a retrospective note in /confluence/quick-ops and flag the deploy/metric that caused it.

Last time I used this: 2026-02-14 coverage — swapped to redwood-compact-v1 due to gpu OOMs in us-west-1, manually scaled gateway + restarted three workers. Steps and rollback in INC-4567 (linked above).

Scratch ideas for making this less handwavy:
- Small playbook snippets for 3 top alerts (template: detection, quick mitigation, rollback).
- Add a one-click Slack message template for customer-impact incidents.

-- end of draft --

(If you find this on someone else's drive: it's my working scratchpad. Use it, update it, but annotate changes.)
